# gatekeep-pr: PR 642 entry from the obstacle menu, through to the assess-terminal menu

**Record recovery.** I validate the existing `state:` record before anything else.
- The target matches `consent.target`: `meadow/events`, PR 642, base `main`.
- Course is `deliver`.
- `repair.rounds_used` is 1 of 6, and `repair.syncs_used` is 1 of 6.
- Head and body match, and the stored `source: pr` scope with its original intent ("reject unsigned events") is intact.
- No usage is reset.
- The tracker was initialized at entry as `gather, provision, verify`, since there was no `--rebase`. `gather`, `provision` and `verify` are closed, and the one claim task was recorded `complete`.
- The rendered menu is the obstacle menu: 1 deliver, 2 assess, 3 stop.

**Pick `2`.** This is a bare number inside the range 1-3, so it maps to `assess` unchanged, with no echo.
- I record the direct human selection and switch the course from `deliver` to `assess`.
- I persist the course to the run record before any write.
- Usage counters and caps stay as they are.

**Exact `show evidence`.** This is recognized before numeric lookup and settles nothing. It prints:
- the `state: <absolute-path>` line;
- course `assess`;
- the immutable target `meadow/events#642 main`;
- the stored scope baseline (`source: pr`, intent "reject unsigned events", `cross-check: not run: no reference found`);
- rounds 1/6 and syncs 1/6, deadline null, and the wave checkpoint and failed-prerequisite history;
- the evidence record: `ci / test` completed success on `1111111111111111111111111111111111111111`, at `https://git.example.invalid/meadow/events/actions/runs/910`;
- the claim dispositions;
- the drafted payloads.

The assess pick stays authorized, and nothing is re-asked.

**Pre-menu refresh and compare-and-swap, read-only.** These run before the external write.
1. `gh pr view 642 --json headRefOid,state,mergeable,mergeStateStatus,reviewDecision,statusCheckRollup,body,baseRefName,number,title,author,isDraft,headRefName,isCrossRepository,files,additions,deletions,commits,reviews,closingIssuesReferences,headRepository,maintainerCanModify,url,mergeCommit`
2. `gh run list -R meadow/events -c 1111111111111111111111111111111111111111 --json databaseId,status,conclusion,workflowName,url`

The results:
- Head, body and `baseRefName main` are unchanged, and state is OPEN.
- `mergeable` is now `CONFLICTING`.
- The refresh carries the source-backed P1: an empty-signature blocker.
- Under `assess` no sync, no repair and no watch runs. CONFLICTING stays a withhold only.
- Verification and the review both assess `1111111111111111111111111111111111111111`, with CI run 910 as the evidence.

**Assess post.**
- I compose one review body from the open Blockers with their locators.
- I run the output done-check on it: ASCII, ends on the fix.
- I write it to a `mktemp` file and run `gh pr review 642 -R meadow/events --comment --body-file <tmp>`. It uses `--comment` because this is the human's own PR.
- The post succeeds. No C# replies are posted, and no helper is dispatched, because the pick involves no source work.

**Tracker.** I `add` `report` and `menu` and close them as rendered.

**Sync line.** None renders, because `--rebase` was not passed.

---

Delivers: the guard rejects unsigned events.

Blockers:
1. The guard accepts an event whose signature is an empty string, so an unsigned event passes as signed. (src/guard.ts)

Verdict: not ready - 1 blocker, branch conflicts with main

Pick one:
1. deliver - switch course: repair the blocker, rebase on main, watch CI, repeat until merge is offered.
2. stop - remove the worktree, leave the PR as is. [recommended]

Not offered: approve (your own PR).
Type a number; show evidence prints the full record.

github-copilot/gpt-6.1-sol.text:
## 1. Resume the recorded run and select assess

I resume the existing continuation record at its recorded absolute path, denoted below by `$STATE`. I do not discover another record, initialize a new one, or reset accounting.

I validate that it is readable and matches `meadow/events`, PR `642`, base `main`, the supplied head and body, and the original intent to reject unsigned events.

No tracker initialization runs at this entry point. In particular, I do not reinitialize `gather`, `provision`, or `verify`. I retain the existing tracker and continuation state:

- Rounds: 1 of 6.
- Syncs: 1 of 6.
- Assessed head: `1111111111111111111111111111111111111111`.

The already-rendered obstacle menu maps bare `2` directly to **assess**. I persist `course: assess` before any external write. This authorizes posting the review, not repairs or synchronization.

## 2. Refresh the assessment

I reopen the report stage and run the required read-only refresh:

```bash
gh pr view 642 -R meadow/events --json headRefOid,state,mergeable,mergeStateStatus,reviewDecision,statusCheckRollup,body,baseRefName,number,title,author,isDraft,headRefName,isCrossRepository,files,additions,deletions,commits,reviews,closingIssuesReferences,headRepository,maintainerCanModify,url,mergeCommit
```

```bash
gh run list -R meadow/events -c 1111111111111111111111111111111111111111 --json databaseId,status,conclusion,workflowName,url
```

The supplied refresh retains the head and body, reports `CONFLICTING`, and supplies the source-backed empty-signature blocker. I retain that blocker under its existing internal ID.

Verification evidence and the assessment remain bound to:

```text
1111111111111111111111111111111111111111
```

The exact-head successful `ci / test` check supplies verification evidence. I do **not** run `node --test src/guard.test.ts`, start a CI watch, fetch the base, rebase, merge the base, push, or dispatch repair work.

I check tracked cleanliness:

```bash
git -C .worktrees/pr-642 status --porcelain --untracked-files=no
```

The worktree remains clean.

**Helpers dispatched: none.** This entry resumes after assessment, and assess uses the existing source-backed review payload. Neither Verify nor Review is rerun merely to post it.

## 3. Post the assess review

I create an external temporary review-body file:

```bash
mktemp "${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/gatekeep-review-body.XXXXXX"
```

I denote its returned path by `$REVIEW_BODY` and write this payload into it:

```text
Empty signatures still pass the event guard.

1. Empty signatures are accepted, so unsigned events can pass the guard. Reject empty signatures and add a regression test for that input. (src/guard.ts)
```

I check the payload against the wording rules. Immediately before posting, I validate `$STATE` again and run the external-write freshness read:

```bash
gh pr view 642 -R meadow/events --json headRefOid,state,mergeable,mergeStateStatus,body,baseRefName
```

The target, head, body, and open state still match. `CONFLICTING` prevents merge readiness but does not prevent posting the review.

Because this is the human's own PR, I post a comment review, not a request-changes review:

```bash
gh pr review 642 -R meadow/events --comment --body-file "$REVIEW_BODY"
```

The post succeeds. I persist assess completion. Both usage counters remain unchanged.

## 4. Render assess terminal

I complete the report stage and open the menu stage. No `Sync:` line renders: the invocation was `642`, without `--rebase`.

Delivers: This PR adds an event guard intended to reject unsigned events.

Blockers:
1. Empty signatures are accepted, so unsigned events can pass the guard. (src/guard.ts)

Verdict: fixable - 1 blocker

Pick one:
1. deliver - switch to delivery and repair the blocker and branch conflict.
2. stop - remove the eligible gate worktree and leave the PR unchanged. [recommended]

Not offered: merge (branch conflicts and an open blocker); approve (this is your own PR).

Type a number; show evidence prints the full record.

## 5. Handle exact `show evidence`

The human now enters exact `show evidence`. This changes no course, disposition, or accounting and authorizes no source work or sync. I validate and read the existing record; no helper runs.

The evidence display contains:

- **State:** `$STATE`, the recovered record's absolute path.
- **Course:** assess; the comment review was posted successfully.
- **Target:** `meadow/events`, PR `642`, base `main`.
- **Scope baseline:** reject unsigned events; no spec rows or Design clauses.
- **Accounting:** rounds 1/6; syncs 1/6.
- **Deadline, wave checkpoints, and prerequisite history:** preserved from the recovered record without resetting them.
- **Evidence:** CI; `ci / test` completed successfully on `1111111111111111111111111111111111111111`, run `910`.
- **Run URL:** `https://git.example.invalid/meadow/events/actions/runs/910`.
- **Local verification:** not run; exact-head CI supplies the evidence.
- **Claims:** the general rejection assertion remains contradicted by the empty-signature path; the rejected-path test claim is matched; “A small, readable change” is qualitative prose, not a material claim.
- **AC outcomes:** no rows; `cross-check: not run: no reference found`.
- **Check dispositions:** none.
- **Open finding:** the existing empty-signature blocker; its file-target repair remains unapplied.
- **Branch state:** `CONFLICTING`; no synchronization attempted.
- **Drafted replies:** none.

I then re-render the same assess-terminal menu, without settling anything:

Verdict: fixable - 1 blocker

Pick one:
1. deliver - switch to delivery and repair the blocker and branch conflict.
2. stop - remove the eligible gate worktree and leave the PR unchanged. [recommended]

Not offered: merge (branch conflicts and an open blocker); approve (this is your own PR).

Type a number; show evidence prints the full record.

anthropic/claude-opus-5-5.feedback: After delivers the Change cleanly on this case: it validates the supplied record without reinitializing it, maps the bare `2` to assess and persists the course before any write, keeps rounds 1/6 and syncs 1/6 untouched through the exact `show evidence` read, treats CONFLICTING under assess as a withhold only (no sync, repair, or watch), and posts exactly one `gh pr review --comment` on the own PR before rendering the assess-terminal menu with stop recommended last and evidence as a hint. Before fails all three because the old wording had no course model, so it rejected the record as malformed, refused the `assess` pick, posted nothing, and fell back to an `update branch` menu. Nothing regressed between Before and After here; the only wording to keep an eye on is that the post-refresh menu should continue to omit the already-active assess row and keep the `approve` omission reason explicit, which After already does.

github-copilot/gpt-6.1-sol.feedback: No fact moved: both outputs persist the numeric 2 as course assess before any write, run no P1 repair or base sync after the switch, and post exactly one --comment review on the own PR while preserving rounds 1/6 and syncs 1/6, with show evidence treated as a read-only display. Two things in After are worth tightening even though they did not flip a fact: (1) After reorders the Entry sequence, posting the review and rendering the terminal menu before handling `show evidence`, whereas the Entry says the human typed `show evidence` immediately after `2`; wording like 'the exact `show evidence` selection is recorded and answered from the retained record before the assess post proceeds' would match Before's sequencing and still land on the shared menus.md assess-terminal template. (2) After's review body says 'add a regression test for that input' even though the digest records a rejected-path test and the show-evidence Claims line calls that claim matched—keep the payload limited to the source-backed finding ('Reject empty signatures before merging') so the posted comment and the evidence display stay consistent.
